name: Aldrete score
seoDesc: Aldrete score: work out circulation from the aldrete score. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Aldrete score calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 5 fields it asks for and it works out circulation straight away, with the formula shown underneath. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Change one value and the results step aside until you press Calculate again, which is what makes it easy to see how much the answer really depends on that one input.

sections.title: How does the Aldrete score calculator work?
sections.html:
The Aldrete score calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports circulation in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the consciousness, the mobility and the breathing); then you type in the aldrete score.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as fully awake, arousable and not responding. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as able to move 4 extremities, able to move 2 extremities and unable to move extremities. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as able to breathe/cough freely, dyspnoea and apnoeic. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as normal, pale/dusky/blotchy/jaundiced and cyanotic. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A number, expressed in pts.

5 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Aldrete score calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Circulation=aldrete score − breathing − color − consciousness − mobility

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
The form opens with a complete set of values: Consciousness set to Fully awake, Mobility set to Able to move 4 extremities, Breathing set to Able to breathe/cough freely and Circulation set to BP ±20%. Straight away the calculator returns Aldrete score = 10.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Aldrete score = 10 should be roughly the size you expected from Consciousness set to Fully awake and Mobility set to Able to move 4 extremities.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• The option the calculation settles on.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Aldrete score calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the aldrete score — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Aldrete score calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns circulation, derived from the aldrete score. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Aldrete score calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the aldrete score, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (5 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Aldrete score = 10. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Aldrete score calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
